newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bond prices ended lower, while rates on shorter maturities rose abruptly.
Swiss short-term rates were seen higher as the Swiss franc weakened, taking some speculation out of the market concerning further declines in Swiss money market rates.

Some traders may have been betting that the Swiss National Bank would continue to lower money rates further if the Swiss franc gained, after the SNB said May 21 it would aggressively add liquidity to the market to offset the Swiss franc's recent rise. Since then, the SNB has cut rates on its daily money operations to 1.00 percent from 1-5/8 percent in early May.
Swiss National Bank president Hans Meyer told journalists at a management conference in Interlaken that the SNB does not target a specific foreign exchange rate, but stayed flexible.
The SNB has never said it did target a certain rate. But the market is usually in a state of watchfulness when the mark dips much below 83.00 Swiss centimes.
Trade was generally calm in the afternoon, after what one Swiss-based trader described as sales which verged on panic during morning, continuing Tuesday's selling trend.
"There was a little panic in the morning, then we calmed down around midday," he said.
The spread between Swiss 10-year and German 10-year federal bonds also continued to narrow, coming in to 236 basis points from 240 late Tuesday, and levels over 250 in recent sessions.
